header: Date: 2027-07-29 | Start: 15:00 PDT | Duration: 46m | Location: Zoom | Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Carlos (Redwood CSM); Maya (Aurora Procurement), Ethan (Aurora Legal), Laura (Aurora Head of ML), Samir (Aurora Cloud Ops)
summary: Procurement-focused call to close MSA/DPA redlines, confirm SLA targets and pricing for committed Dedicated capacity, and align on onboarding timeline. Key items: redlined MSA data residency language, SLA appendix with latency and availability targets, pricing tiers and committed GPU pool sizing, SOC2/KMS questions answered. Agreed next steps and dates for contract exchange and onboarding kickoff.
topics: Pricing: committed vs burst, overage billing
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Jordan Patel, AE at Redwood, with Priya our SE and Carlos from CSM. How's everyone doing?
[00:07] Maya: Good thanks. We have legal on; Ethan's here and we'll be focused mostly on the procurement items.
[00:12] Ethan: Yep thanks. We'll try to keep it tight. Main goal is to close MSA redlines and scope SLA.
[00:18] Priya: Great, so I pulled the SLA appendix and the DPA draft. I know there were two main asks: data residency and stronger audit log language, and then some clarifications on KMS/hsm.
[00:30] Laura: Correct, for HIPAA/PHI workloads we need to confirm that customer data can be restricted to our AWS account in eu-west-1 and that logs are retained per our policy.
[00:40] Samir: Also want to understand key management - do we have a bring-your-own-key option or is it Redwood-managed?
[00:47] Jordan: Short answer: for Private deployments we support customer-managed KMS and HSM integrations. For Dedicated hosted we're offering a customer-dedicated tenant with Redwood-managed keys by default but BYOK is on the table for enterprise. We'll put exact options into the DPA.
[01:02] Ethan: Okay, good. The redline we sent asked for explicit KMS language and an audit right. We also flagged termination data return and deletion timelines.
[01:10] Priya: We can commit to 30 days for data return and 90 days for deletion verifiable reports; we will add deletion certificates and the audit log exports. That's consistent with our enterprise playbook.
[01:24] Maya: On the MSA there was a data residency clause we asked for - that processing and storage is limited to eu-west-1 for all production data.
[01:32] Jordan: We can add a residency clause for production datasets for Dedicated customers. For Hosted API customers that's trickier, but for the Dedicated pool we can pin region. We'll reflect that in the MSA appendix and the DPA - note: the language may say 'to the extent technically feasible' - legal might push back on that.
[01:48] Ethan: We prefer concrete promise vs 'to the extent' language. Can Redwood put an SLA credit for breach of residency?
[01:55] Jordan: We can propose an availability-style credit or a compliance credit; need to confirm internally. Priya, do we have precedent?
[02:02] Priya: We've done region-pinning for a handful of Dedicated customers and included a remedy clause; we rarely see region breach, so a credit tied to verified breach should be okay but I want to confirm with product.
[02:12] Carlos: We'll log that as an action - Jordan to propose compliance credit language.
[02:16] Samir: On SLAs, Aurora needs 99.9% monthly availability and p50 latency < 200ms for standard generation on our typical prompt size. Can Redwood commit to that on Dedicated?
[02:27] Priya: 99.9% is reasonable for Dedicated committed pools; latency commitments depend on model and seq length. For our reference models we have p50 under 150ms at typical QPS, but we'll include a perf appendix with measured percentiles and fallbacks to smaller models if needed.
[02:41] Laura: Fallbacks are fine as long as we get an explicit notice and the output quality is within agreed bounds. We need versioning and the ability to pin model major versions.
[02:50] Priya: Yes, the deployment layer supports model pinning and can roll back. We'll add that to the rollout section.
[02:56] Maya: Pricing - we were quoted committed capacity for 4 GPUs for 12 months. Proc has asked for pricing tiers and an overage rate if we burst beyond committed.
[03:05] Jordan: The spreadsheet we'll send shows committed monthly units, base price per GPU-hour, and an overage multiplier (1.8x for burst). We also have a blended discount for longer terms.
[03:15] Ethan: On overage billing, need clarity on how continuous batching and caching impact token accounting - we don't want double-billing.
[03:22] Priya: Tokens consumed are measured server-side after dedup and cache hits; the billing metric is net tokens served. We'll include measurement examples in the pricing sheet so you can see how caching reduces cost.
[03:34] Samir: Security controls - SOC2 report? SSO? RBAC?
[03:38] Jordan: We are SOC2 Type II. SSO is supported via SAML/Okta. RBAC and fine-grained API keys with route permissions are part of the platform. We'll attach SOC2 report and the security whitepaper.
[03:50] Ethan: Need to confirm log retention retention times for audit - we require 365 days for audit logs.
[03:55] Priya: We can provide 365 days export of audit logs as an add-on; include in DPA appendix.
[04:02] Maya: Cool. Onboard timeline is critical - legal wants contracts signed before end of August to hit our Q4 roadmap.
[04:09] Jordan: Our proposed timeline: send redlined MSA/DPA by 8/5, customer to return by 8/12, sign by 8/19, kick off onboarding week of 8/22. Does that align?
[04:20] Ethan: That timeline is tight but doable if there are no new material asks.
[04:24] Laura: We also want a quick benchmark run: 1k sample calls to validate latency on our prompts before sign. Can Redwood run that?
[04:33] Priya: Yes - we can run a benchmark run in staged Dedicated pool or with a perf harness against a compatible model. We'll need a test dataset and agreed SLOs.
[04:42] Samir: We'll share sample prompts and expected seq lengths by EOD tomorrow.
[04:45] Jordan: Great. Any other open procurement items?
[04:48] Maya: Procurement will need the redlined MSA, final pricing spreadsheet, and SOC2 before we can issue PO.
[04:54] Carlos: We'll bundle all that: MSA/DPA redlines, pricing, SOC2, onboarding checklist.
[04:59] Ethan: One more legal ask - indemnity carveouts on third party model IP. If Redwood uses third-party open models, we need assurances around IP.
[05:07] Priya: We can include model provenance language and warranty limited to willful misconduct; for open models we provide best-effort provenance. Legal teams often accept model-usage disclaimers but we'll add the language and flag for product/legal review.
[05:22] Jordan: Ok I'll coordinate with product/legal for a final clause.
[05:26] Maya: Perfect. So next steps recap?
[05:29] Jordan: Jordan to send revised MSA + DPA with data residency and compliance credit proposal by 8/5; Priya to send SLA appendix and perf spreadsheet by 8/2; Carlos to send onboarding checklist and SOC2 attestation; Aurora will send test prompts by tomorrow and legal to review redlines by 8/12.
[05:45] Ethan: Thanks everyone. We'll review and push for signoff as long as the language is tight.
[05:50] Jordan: Thanks all, we'll follow up in email with the artifacts.
[05:53] Maya: Thanks, bye.
[05:55] End of call
